teams.heading: Jamie George says Times rift report is 'untrue' ahead of Wallabies
teams.body: Jamie George says the squad are "really upset" by a Times report claiming England's July tour was marked by player unrest over head coach Steve Borthwick's leadership. The report says unhappy players wanted summit talks with Borthwick and RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney in Argentina. "I can tell you that a lot of it's untrue," he told Rugby Union Weekly, querying the timing two days before the Wallabies. George said: "This is going to galvanise us."

lead.why: It is a new England squad story about a newspaper report on player unrest, and the hooker's on-record rebuttal is the most talked-about item in the pack.

teams.heading: France average 38.7 points a game across their last 11 matches
teams.body: France's scoring over their last 11 games stands at 426 points, with 291 conceded. That works out at 38.7 points scored and 26.5 conceded per game across the window. Their biggest win in that run was 54-12 away to Wales in February's Six Nations. Their most recent result was a 42-15 win over Japan, and Fiji are next.

teams.heading: Hugo Keenan hat-trick fires Ireland to six-try 42-12 win over Argentina
teams.body: Friday's win at the Aviva Stadium was built on Hugo Keenan's three tries, but head coach Andy Farrell wanted more. Ireland's six tries also came from Dan Sheehan, Sam Prendergast and Ronan Kelleher, yet they did not score after the 55th minute. "I thought there was outstanding stuff and some clinical stuff, but I think the story of the game is we missed a chance to be ruthless," Farrell said. Robert Baloucoune left with a knock, and Mack Hansen had treatment for an ankle.

lead.why: A fresh match result that gives Ireland's six-try win and Farrell's verdict on it a clear Ireland angle, and it is not one of the stories already run on this tab.

teams.heading: Quesada welcomes back Capuozzo, names Nicotera captain without Lamaro against Springboks
teams.body: Azzurri head coach Gonzalo Quesada has named his side for the Nations Championship clash with world champions South Africa in Turin without captain Michele Lamaro, Tommaso Menoncello or Juan Ignacio Brex, all sidelined. Hooker Giacomo Nicotera leads the team in Lamaro's absence, while wing Ange Capuozzo returns to start for the first time since the Six Nations. Paolo Garbisi and Alessandro Fusco renew their half-back partnership. Italy are missing 16 players through injury, according to the federation's preview.

teams.heading: Townsend restores Russell and Tuipulotu to start against All Blacks
teams.body: Finn Russell returns at fly-half and captain Sione Tuipulotu at centre, both missing from the Fiji win in July. Rory Sutherland is the only forward retained from the Fiji side, and vice-captain Rory Darge is back. Saturday's Test is the first of four this month for Scotland. Townsend says New Zealand are "playing much more ambitious rugby." Scotland have never beaten the All Blacks.

teams.heading: Alex Mann starts against Japan as fans question his physical profile
teams.body: Cardiff's Alex Mann is in Wales' side for Saturday's Nations Championship match with Japan. WalesOnline's Steffan Thomas writes that much of the criticism he attracts centres on his physical profile, with some supporters preferring a bigger presence. Wales' coaching staff and team-mates rate him highly. His relentless defensive work, the report says, frees Jac Morgan and Aaron Wainwright to carry more in the wider channels. One unnamed coach says the 24-year-old shows little regard for his own wellbeing when putting his body on the line.

lead.why: It is a new, Wales-specific item about a named starter, and it is not already in the reader's previous editions.

teams.heading: Pumas slump to third defeat in four as Hugo Keenan nets hat-trick
teams.body: Ireland beat Argentina 42-12 at the Aviva Stadium, with Hugo Keenan scoring three of their six tries. Two Argentina players were sin-binned, and captain Julian Montoya was lost to a failed head injury assessment before half-time. Mateo Carreras scored both Argentina tries, but Ireland led 21-5 at the break. The defeat leaves Argentina with three losses in four games, with trips to Italy and France to come.

lead.why: A fresh match result that Argentina's own edition can frame from the Pumas' side, and the most-covered new item in the pack.

teams.heading: Josh Canham, son of English parents, starts at lock against England
teams.body: Born in the United States and in Melbourne from the age of eight, Canham has become one of the breakthrough players of Les Kiss's season. His English parents were "50-50" about which team he would play for, he told AAP, and the 25-year-old said: "I felt Australian and I am Australian, so playing for the Wallabies has always been my dream." He spoke with Northampton early in his career but stayed in Australia, and as the established line-out caller he starts in Sunday's tight five.

teams.heading: Kingsley Jones, ex-Wales international, back in Japan camp this week
teams.body: Kingsley Jones, who left Canada's head-coach job last year, has spent this week in Japan's camp, Eddie Jones said on Thursday. The coach joked, "He can talk, mate!", before adding that he was there to watch and feed back on how Japan can improve. Japan's coach also met Wales coach Steve Tandy at a world rugby coaches' conference this week and says he has a good idea how Wales will play. Japan's onus, he said, is to disrupt that gameplan at the Principality Stadium on Saturday.

teams.heading: Planet Rugby tips All Blacks to beat Scotland at Murrayfield on Saturday
teams.body: Planet Rugby's preview expects a tricky afternoon rather than a formality, with the forward battle likely to decide it. Scotland are yet to beat New Zealand, who have won 31 of their 33 meetings, but they have lost the last four by eight points or fewer. The piece highlights set-piece work as the key area: New Zealand conceded 14 penalties and a penalty try from the set-piece in the 3-1 series defeat to South Africa, while Scotland's scrummaging has improved.

teams.heading: Siya Kolisi says Boks have not yet taken in Hyron Andrews' death
teams.body: Siya Kolisi, speaking from Turin, says the squad is still coming to terms with the sudden death of former teammate Hyron Andrews in France on 16 October. "I don't think it sank in for a lot of us because it feels like we were just with Hyron the other day," the Bok skipper said. He called Andrews "an amazing human being" and said he could not imagine what it was like for his widow, Maiglin, and their sons.

lead.why: It is a new South Africa story from the squad itself, with the captain speaking directly about a teammate's death.
